subject.title: fix(auto-reply): retry reply-session init CAS conflicts with backoff

question: Should all inbound paths treat session-init CAS conflicts as a bounded transient retry at the common session layer, accepting an error after exhaustion, or must message-bearing paths durably re-enqueue until delivery is resolved?
rationale: The common retry removes channel asymmetry with minimal duplication, but its exhaustion behavior can still silently lose a non-spooled inbound event; source inspection cannot determine the intended delivery guarantee.

options.title: Bounded common retry
options.body: Use the common unlocked retry, fix abort handling, and explicitly accept that sustained conflicts can still return an error after five attempts.

options.title: Durable inbound recovery
options.body: Require message-bearing callers to spool or re-enqueue exhausted conflicts so an inbound event is not discarded after the bounded source retry.

recommendation.title: Bounded common retry
recommendation.body: Use the common unlocked retry, fix abort handling, and explicitly accept that sustained conflicts can still return an error after five attempts.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly related current-main work established the source-side serialization boundary that this retry extends.
